# EggMapper — full reference for AI coding assistants

Fast .NET object mapper with AutoMapper's API. Package `EggMapper` (runtime, includes DI). Compile-time tiers:
`EggMapper.Generator` (`[MapTo]`) and `EggMapper.ClassMapper` (`[EggMapper]` partial classes). Targets netstandard2.0,
net462, net8.0-net11.0. License MIT OR Apache-2.0. Short version: llms.txt.

## Rules that save round trips

- Register maps in `Profile` classes; scan with `cfg.AddMaps(assembly)` or `services.AddEggMapper(assembly)`.
- Prefer `mapper.Map<S, D>(src)`; inject `IMapper<S, D>` on hot paths.
- Keep one `MapperConfiguration` (singleton). Maps compile on first use; `CompileMappings()` compiles all.
- Add one test calling `CompileMappings()` and `AssertConfigurationIsValid()`.
- `ProjectTo<S, D>(config)` needs both type arguments.
- Read error messages: they name the missing `CreateMap` or member.

## Configuration and mapping

```csharp compile
public class Address { public string Street { get; set; } = ""; public string City { get; set; } = ""; }
public class Person
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
    public string FirstName { get; set; } = "";
    public string LastName { get; set; } = "";
    public Address Address { get; set; } = new();
    public string? Nickname { get; set; }
}
public class PersonDto
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
    public string FullName { get; set; } = "";
    public string AddressCity { get; set; } = "";
    public string Nickname { get; set; } = "";
    public string Secret { get; set; } = "";
}
public record PersonSummary(int Id, string FirstName);

public class PersonProfile : Profile
{
    public PersonProfile()
    {
        CreateMap<Person, PersonDto>()
            .ForMember(d => d.FullName, o => o.MapFrom(s => s.FirstName + " " + s.LastName))
            .ForMember(d => d.Nickname, o => o.NullSubstitute("none"))
            .ForMember(d => d.Secret, o => o.Ignore());
        CreateMap<Person, PersonSummary>();
    }
}
```

`AddressCity` maps from `Address.City` by flattening. `PersonSummary` is built through its constructor.

```csharp compile
var config = new MapperConfiguration(cfg => cfg.AddMaps(typeof(PersonProfile).Assembly));
var mapper = config.CreateMapper();
var person = new Person { Id = 1, FirstName = "Ada", LastName = "Lovelace" };

PersonDto dto = mapper.Map<Person, PersonDto>(person);
PersonDto viaObject = mapper.Map<PersonDto>(person);
mapper.Map(person, dto);
List<PersonDto> many = mapper.MapList<Person, PersonDto>(new List<Person> { person });
mapper.Patch(new Person { FirstName = "Grace" }, dto);
Person copy = mapper.Map<Person, Person>(person);
IMapper<Person, PersonDto> typed = config.CreateMapper<Person, PersonDto>();
PersonDto fast = typed.Map(person);
```

`Map<T, T>` works without a `CreateMap`: it creates a new object and copies members; nested objects keep the same
references. `Patch` skips source members whose value is null (reference types and
`Nullable<T>`); non-nullable value types are always copied.

## Member options

`ForMember(d => d.X, o => ...)`: `MapFrom(s => expr)`, `MapFrom("SourceName")`, `Ignore()`, `Condition(s => bool)`,
`PreCondition(s => bool)`, `NullSubstitute(value)`, `UseValue(value)`, `UseDestinationValue()`,
`MapFrom<TResolver, TSourceMember>(s => s.Member)` (DI resolver). `ForPath(d => d.A.B, o => o.MapFrom(...))` sets a
nested destination member. `ForAllOtherMembers(o => o.Ignore())` ignores everything not configured.

## Map-level options

```csharp compile
var config = new MapperConfiguration(cfg =>
{
    cfg.CreateMap<Order, OrderDto>()
        .BeforeMap((s, d) => d.Note = "")
        .AfterMap((s, d) => d.Total = s.Items.Sum(i => i.Price))
        .ForMember(d => d.CustomerName, o => o.MapFrom(s => s.Customer!.Name))
        .ForMember(d => d.Internal, o => o.Ignore())
        .Validate(d => d.Total, total => total >= 0, "Total must not be negative");
    cfg.CreateMap<OrderItem, OrderItemDto>().ReverseMap();
    cfg.CreateMap<Product, ProductDto>().ConvertUsing(p => new ProductDto { Id = p.Id });
    cfg.AddTypeConverter<DateTime, string>(d => d.ToString("O"));
    cfg.ShouldMapProperty = p => p.Name != "Internal";
});
config.CompileMappings();
```

Also: `ConstructUsing(s => new D(...))`, `IncludeBase<SBase, DBase>()` (inherit a base map's configuration),
`MaxDepth(n)` (self-referencing types), `CreateMap(typeof(Page<>), typeof(PageDto<>))` (open generics),
`ConvertUsing<TConverter>()` with `ITypeConverter<S, D>`, call-site options
`mapper.Map<S, D>(src, opts => opts.AfterMap((s, d) => ...))` with `opts.Items`.

## Enums

Different enum types map by name (exact, then ignoring case, else by value), like AutoMapper.
`cfg.EnumMapping = EnumMappingMode.ByValue` restores numeric mapping. Per pair:
`CreateMap<EA, EB>().ConvertUsingEnumMapping(o => o.MapByName().MapValue(EA.X, EB.Y))`. Enum <-> string and int <-> enum
convert automatically. `ProjectTo` maps enums by value.

## Dependency injection

```csharp compile
services.AddEggMapper(typeof(OrderItemDto).Assembly);
services.AddEggMapper(cfg => cfg.CreateMap<Order, OrderDto>());
```

Registers `MapperConfiguration` (singleton), `IMapper` and `IMapper<S, D>` (transient; each carries the scope's
`IServiceProvider`, so DI value resolvers get scoped services).

## IQueryable projection

```csharp compile
var config = new MapperConfiguration(cfg => cfg.CreateMap<Product, ProductDto>());
IQueryable<ProductDto> query = products.ProjectTo<Product, ProductDto>(config);
```

Translatable members only: same-name, flattened, nested registered maps, `MapFrom` expressions. Child collections,
converters and resolvers are skipped.

## Compile-time tiers (separate packages)

```csharp
[MapTo(typeof(OrderDto))]          // EggMapper.Generator: generates order.ToOrderDto()
public class Order { /* ... */ }

[EggMapper]                        // EggMapper.ClassMapper: generates the method bodies
public partial class OrderMapper
{
    public partial OrderDto Map(Order source);
}
```

Analyzer EGG1003 suggests `[MapTo]` for `CreateMap` calls without customization; EGG1002 flags configurations never
validated.

## Differences from AutoMapper

| AutoMapper | EggMapper |
|---|---|
| `ProjectTo<D>(cfg)` | `ProjectTo<S, D>(cfg)` |
| `mapper.ConfigurationProvider` | keep the `MapperConfiguration` instance |
| `ForCtorParam` | constructor parameters match source members by name; else `ConstructUsing` |
| `ForSourceMember`, `IncludeMembers` | not supported; use `ForMember` with `MapFrom` |
| `Include<,>`, `As<>`, polymorphic dispatch | not supported; `IncludeAllDerived()` only shares base configuration |
| `IValueResolver<S, D, M>` | `IMemberValueResolver<S, D, TSourceMember, M>` with `MapFrom<TResolver, TSourceMember>` |
| `ReverseMap()` inverting `MapFrom` / unflattening | convention-only reverse map; configure it with its own `CreateMap` |
| AutoMapper licence (commercial from v15) | MIT OR Apache-2.0 |

## Errors and fixes

| Message | Fix |
|---|---|
| `No mapping configured for S -> D` | `cfg.CreateMap<S, D>()`; for a list, the element map |
| `Unmapped destination member 'D.X' in map S -> D` | `.ForMember(d => d.X, o => o.MapFrom(s => ...))` or `o.Ignore()` |
| `MappingValidationException` | a `Validate` rule failed; the message lists every failed rule |
| `MappingException` wrapping another error | the inner exception names the cause; check `MapFrom` expressions |
| `Circular IncludeBase() reference` | remove the cycle between `IncludeBase` calls |

## Performance

Benchmarks (BenchmarkDotNet, .NET 10) are in the README and regenerated by CI on every merge:
https://github.com/eggspot/EggMapper#performance
